author: cosminperram
body:
Adds the option (enabled by default) to cache ports.

This is the most beneficial when you query the same server (identified by resolved address and port) and it doesn't end up successful on the first attempted port (e.g. specify the query port without `--givenPortOnly` or games that might have multiple offsets (soon to come)).

An example of this would be:
Query `DayZ` server A (with 1 maximum attempt), where we know the query port of that specific server (P1):
1st attempt: specified port + offset (P2)... failure.
2nd attempt: specified port (P1)... success. -- add this port as cached.

Some time later, query the same server (A) with the same port (P1):
1st attempt: cached port... success.

It would only regress if the server changes the query port whilst your service is running, which is not very likely but the other edge cases heavily outweigh this.

This replaces #454, that PR introduces backwards-compatibility regressions by always trying the specified user port firstly, as many users of [Homepage](https://github.com/gethomepage/homepage) or [Uptime Kuma](https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma) just put in their default connect port. The attempt order ends up with the first attempted port to be the specified port and the offset, the PR would change this behaviour by making the user given port the first one, making these queries slower with the extra attempt.

This caused us to need to update the version of breathe we rely on to build the compiler documentation. - sphinxcontrib-chapeldomain from 0.0.28 to 0.0.29

author: hebarusan
body:
## Problem

The Contents tab refreshes and shows the mod contents if you download a mod via the Download button or right click menu, but not if it is downloaded during installation.

## Cause

Refreshing cache-related state (including the Contents tab) is handled (duplicatively) at the places where GUI stores or purges a mod, but when you install an uncached mod, it is downloaded and stored by `ModuleInstaller`, so GUI doesn't react.

This is a brittle approach because it has a many-to-many structure, where each place that deals with the cache must also handle all of the secondary consequences itself.

## Changes

- Now `NetModuleCache` has `ModStored` and `ModPurged` events that it fires whenever mods are stored or purged, including during mod installation. If **all** mods are purged, `ModPurged`'s module parameter will be null.
- The logic for reacting to cache changes is consolidated into one `GUI.Main.OnModStoredOrPurged` function, which is used to handle the new events, including during installation. Places that formerly triggered the refresh now no longer do, because they don't need to anymore.
- `UpdateCachedByDownloads` can now handle updating the full mod list's `IsCached` property when its parameter is `null`, for when the user clears the cache in the settings
- `ManageMods.OnSelectedModuleChanged` now no longer sets ModInfo's active mod when the Manage Mods tab is not active, for when `OnModStoredOrPurged` refilters the mod list in the background during installs, because this causes ModInfo to become visible when it shouldn't. It will still be set when the Manage Mods tab becomes active again.

Fixes #3998.

## Description

Modifies the credential expiry service to accept a new `SCANNER_V4` component which when used will cause Central to contact the `indexer` and `matcher` endpoints to retrieve the associated certificates. The expiry of the 'oldest' (soonest to expire) certificate will be returned.

The credential expiry service is used by the ACS UI on the `System Health` page.


## Checklist
- [x] Investigated and inspected CI test results
- [X] Unit test and regression tests added
- [ ] ~Evaluated and added CHANGELOG entry if required~
- [ ] ~Determined and documented upgrade steps~
- [ ] ~Documented user facing changes (create PR based on [openshift/openshift-docs](https://github.com/openshift/openshift-docs) and merge into [rhacs-docs](https://github.com/openshift/openshift-docs/tree/rhacs-docs))~

If any of these don't apply, please comment below.

## Testing Performed

On an OCP infra cluster, installed Central Services with Scanner V4 enabled, and then tested interactions via the ACS API:

```
$ time curl -ks -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://$ACS_HOST/v1/credentialexpiry?component=SCANNER_V4
{"expiry":"2025-01-15T16:35:53Z"}
real    0m0.266s
user    0m0.011s
sys     0m0.018s

# Central logs
credentialexpiry/service: 2024/01/16 19:54:50.569217 service_impl.go:212: Debug: Obtained expiry for "Scanner V4 Indexer": 2025-01-15T16:35:53Z
credentialexpiry/service: 2024/01/16 19:54:50.573428 service_impl.go:212: Debug: Obtained expiry for "Scanner V4 Matcher": 2025-01-15T16:35:53Z

```

To verify have default timeouts, adjusted the `scanner-v4-matcher` `netpol` to block requests from central and retested:

```
$ k edit netpol scanner-v4-matcher
$ time curl -ks -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://$ACS_HOST/v1/credentialexpiry?component=SCANNER_V4
{"expiry":"2025-01-15T16:35:53Z"}
real    2m10.456s
user    0m0.018s
sys     0m0.023s

# Central logs
credentialexpiry/service: 2024/01/16 19:55:28.950550 service_impl.go:212: Debug: Obtained expiry for "Scanner V4 Indexer": 2025-01-15T16:35:53Z
pkg/tlsutils: 2024/01/16 19:57:38.527134 dial_context.go:22: Debug: tls dial failed{error 26 0  dial tcp 10.131.0.27:8443: connect: connection timed out}
```

Reverted the `netpol` changes and then shutdown matcher to ensure that as long as one of indexer/matcher is available can still get results:
```
$ k edit netpol scanner-v4-matcher
$ k scale deploy/scanner-v4-matcher --replicas=0
$ time curl -ks -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://$ACS_HOST/v1/credentialexpiry?component=SCANNER_V4
{"expiry":"2025-01-15T16:35:53Z"}
real    0m0.257s

```

author: jkarneges
body:
This allows one handler to receive stats from multiple proxies. Proxy instances send most stats types over the stats socket, but they also send conn-max over the accept socket, so the handler needs to be able to connect to multiple of both.

With this change, it is possible to then tell the handler to connect to multiple proxy instances like this:

```
[handler]
...
proxy_accept_specs=ipc://{rundir}/{ipc_prefix}accept-1,ipc://{rundir}/{ipc_prefix}accept-2
proxy_stats_specs=ipc://{rundir}/{ipc_prefix}proxy-stats-1,ipc://{rundir}/{ipc_prefix}proxy-stats-2
```

Notes:

* Running multiple handlers (e.g. N handlers and 1 proxy, or N handlers and M proxies) will result in incorrect stats. This change only enables stats to work with 1 handler and N proxies.
* Other things are broken when running multiple proxies, such as retry and websocket control sessions. This change is just a first step towards eventually getting multiple proxies to work.

![yfcc-10M](https://github.com/harsha-simhadri/big-ann-benchmarks/assets/44047980/270c7925-417f-47dc-80f7-a3b00b71defd)

Our solution is based on vamana graph and tag partition. For each query, we handle it differently according to its tag's cardinality. We construct a vamana graph for every tag with cardinality larger than a threshold. For each query, we search with graph if its cardinality is large and search with brute force if its cardinality is small. Additionally, we organize queries tag by tag to enhance cache locality.
